text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 6 in history:

1475 - Michelangelo Buonarotti, Italian painter, sculptor and architect, born. Described as the most brilliant representative of the Italian Renaissance,he was famed for his work on the Sistine Chapel, his painting of "The Last Judgement" and his statue of "David".
1480 - The Treaty of Toledo was signed under which Spain recognised Portugal's conquest of Morocco and Portugal ceded claims to the Canary Islands.
1619 - Savinien Cyrano de Bergerac, French satirist and dramatist, born.
1834 - The city of Toronto was incorporated with William Lyon Mackenzie as its first mayor.
1836 - The siege of the Alamo ended when Mexican troops under General Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna captured the mission fort garrisoned by Davey Crockett and 154 Texans.
1853 - Verdi's opera "La Traviata" was performed for the first time, in Venice.
1882 - Prince Milan IV proclaimed himself king of Serbia.
1888 - Louisa May Alcott, U.S. novelist and author of "Little Women", died.
1900 - Gottfried Daimler, motor engineer who improved the engine and made the first motorcycle, died.
1932 - John Philip Sousa, U.S. bandmaster and composer of military marches, died.
1941 - U.S. sculptor Gutzon Borglum died. Noted for his work on Mount Rushmore, South Dakota, where he carved the heads of presidents Washington, Jefferson, Lincoln and Theodore Roosevelt.
1944 - U.S. bombers began daytime attacks on Berlin from bases in Britain.
1945 - Tanks and infantry of the U.S. First Army drove into Cologne, Germany.
1951 - Ivor Novello, Welsh composer and playwright, died.
1953 - Georgy Malenkov succeeded Stalin as premier and first secretary of the Soviet Communist Party.
1957 - Ghana became independent within the Commonwealth.
1964 - King Constantine II of Greece succeeded to the throne after the death of his father, Paul I.
1967 - Zoltan Kodaly, Hungarian composer of "Dances of Galanta", died.
1967 - Svetlana Alliluyeva, Stalin's daughter, requested asylum at the U.S. embassy in New Delhi.
1973 - Pearl Buck, U.S. author of "The Good Earth", died; she won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1938.
1980 - Belgian-born French author Marguerite Yourcenar became the first woman writer to be elected to the Academie Francaise.
1983 - Chancellor Helmut Kohl and his Christian Democrats were returned to power in Germany.
1983 - Donald Maclean, former British diplomat and Soviet spy, died in Moscow.
1987 - A Townsend Thoreson ferry, Herald of Free Enterprise, capsized on its way out of Zeebrugge harbour in Belgium drowning 193 people.
1988 - Three members of an Irish Republican Army unit were shot dead in a Gibraltar street by undercover SAS commandos.
1991 - Indian Prime Minister Chandra Shekhar resigned after only four months in office having lost the support of Rajiv Gandhi's Congress (I) party.
1991 - George Carey won formal election to become the next Archbishop of Canterbury and leader of the world's 70 million Anglicans.
1992 - The president of Azerbaijan, Ayaz Mutalibov, resigned over his handling of the conflict in Nagorno-Karabakh.
1992 - Michelangelo, one of the most alarming computer viruses to surface, struck thousands of personal computers around the world.
1994 - Melina Mercouri, Greek actress turned fiery Socialist politician, died after a long battle with lung cancer.
